name: Sam
entries: Moved the last of my stuff out of Jess's place today. Four years and it fit in the back of a Corolla. My sister Mia helped carry boxes and didn't ask anything, which I appreciated. Ate noodles on the floor of the new flat because I don't have a table yet.

Honestly the closest thing to connection today was the guy at the hardware store asking if I was alright. I must look rough. Jess texted asking if I'd taken the blue lamp. I had. I said I'd drop it back. I won't.
Jess. Obviously. I keep replaying the night she said she didn't see a future. I think I knew months ago. I just kept being busy so I didn't have to look at it.

Sunday was heavy. Everyone thinks I'm fine because I keep saying I'm fine. Haven't told anyone how bad the nights are. Thought about whether I should talk to someone professional, but that feels like making it a bigger deal than it is.
Mia came over with a table she found on Marketplace. We built it badly and laughed a lot. First time I've laughed properly in two weeks. She asked about Jess and I changed the subject.
Looking forward to the weekend. I think I'm going to call Mia on Saturday and actually tell her how I'm going, not the fine version. That's the plan anyway.
Better than last week. Slept six hours. Saw a photo of Jess at a gig with friends we used to share and felt sick for an hour, then it passed. It passes faster now.
More of being chosen, I think. I spent the whole relationship trying to be easy to love. Low maintenance. I never asked for much and then I was surprised when I didn't get much.
Work was fine, distracting. Didn't call Mia on Saturday in the end. Told myself she was busy. She wasn't. Jess's birthday is next week and I don't know if I'm supposed to message.
I'm avoiding the idea that I might need actual help with this. Second time I've written that. Maybe I should look up a counsellor. Even typing that feels dramatic.
I'm drawn to people who need fixing a little. Jess was going through a lot when we met. I liked being needed. Then she didn't need me and I didn't know what I was for.
Jess's birthday tomorrow. Decided not to message. Mia's taking me to the beach instead. I told her a bit more today in the car. Not everything, but more.
The beach was good. Mia said she'd worried about me since the move and didn't know how to bring it up. I cried in the car park. Felt lighter after.
Proud I didn't text Jess on her birthday. Proud I let Mia in a bit. Still sad but it's a cleaner kind of sad. Two weeks of writing this. Feels like it's helped me see things.

name: Dan
entries: Standup ran 40 minutes again. Priya, my manager, moved the deadline forward without asking anyone. Spent the afternoon redoing a deck I finished last week. Gym after, which helped.
Honestly the only part that gives me energy is mentoring the grads. Taught Leo how to structure a model today and he got it. Everything else feels like moving numbers between slides.

Priya cc'd her boss on an email pointing out my mistake. It was a small mistake. Felt like a public slap. Didn't say anything. Haven't told anyone about how much this place is getting to me, not even Kate.
What made today feel worthwhile: called my dad Pete about his knee surgery. He's scared but won't say it. We talked footy for twenty minutes. That was the best part of the week.
Drains me: the sense that nothing I do is noticed unless it's wrong. Priya again. Third or fourth time I've written about her now. I lie awake rehearsing conversations I'll never have.
Leo sent me a meme about Excel and I laughed out loud on the train. Small thing. Kate made pasta. A normal good evening.
If money weren't a factor I'd teach. Maths, probably, high school. I keep thinking about it then telling myself it's a pay cut and a fantasy.
Work stress again. Got a vague 'can we chat Monday' from Priya on Friday afternoon. Spent the whole weekend dreading it. Kate asked what was wrong twice. I said tired.
Monday chat was nothing. She wanted me to lead the client workshop. Spent two days catastrophising about a compliment. That's a bit insane when I write it down.
I lose track of time when I'm explaining something to someone and I can see it click. Mentoring Leo. Coaching Dad through his physio app. Teaching, basically. It keeps coming back to that.
Some days I wonder what the point of any of it is. Not in a dark way, more like am I just going to make slides until I'm sixty. Dad's surgery went fine though.
Whose success am I chasing? My dad's, partly. He left school at fifteen and was so proud when I got this job. Teaching would feel like going backwards to him, I think. I've never asked him.

Told Kate about the teaching thing last night. All of it, including Priya. She said she'd noticed I'd gone quiet for months. She didn't think it was crazy. Felt like putting down a bag I didn't know I was carrying.

Proud I ran the client workshop and it went well. Proud I finally told Kate. Looking at a part-time teaching course for next year, just to see. Two weeks in and this has been more useful than I expected.

name: Lena
entries: Dreamt I was in a pottery studio underwater and the clay kept floating away. Weirdly calm though. I've been thinking about signing up for a wheel class, maybe that's why.
Something I'd love to make: a set of mismatched mugs for my flat, each one for a different mood. Grumpy Monday mug. Saturday market mug. Very twee, I know.
Went to the market with Ana. Bought too many tomatoes. We talked about her new job for ages and I realised I never really talk about mine. Not much to say, it's fine.
Booked the pottery class! Thursday nights, six weeks. Told Ana and she wants to come to the first one.
Ana did an impression of our old maths teacher that made me snort tea. We should hang out more. Every time we do I feel more like myself.
Plans: work, then first pottery class. Nervous in a fun way. Haven't done anything new in ages.
Best part: the class. My bowl collapsed three times and the teacher said that's the whole first lesson, learning to fail at the wheel. I loved it.
The idea that keeps coming back is a little stall at the Saturday market. Mugs, plants, maybe zines. It's silly at my skill level but it keeps coming back.
Bit flat today. Rainy, work was dull, didn't see anyone. Nothing wrong, just grey.
What's stopping me starting the stall: honestly, I'm scared people will think it's amateurish. Which it would be. I also haven't told anyone except here.
Second class. Made a cylinder that stood up! Ana came again and said I seemed happier than she's seen in a while.
Something tomorrow that would make me feel good: actually sketching the stall idea instead of just thinking about it.
If no one would judge: hand-painted mugs with tiny weird sentences on the bottom that you only see when you finish your tea. 'You're doing fine.' 'Call your mum.' I love that idea.
Proud of sticking with pottery and writing here every day. Two weeks. Feels like I've got a bit more colour back. Might tell Ana about the stall idea this weekend.
